intended: This class manages the lifecycle of a websocket connection. It handles the initial handshake, sends heartbeats, and reconnects with backoff when the connection drops. The heartbeat interval is 25 seconds, because some proxies close idle connections after 30 seconds. Be careful when changing the backoff logic, because it interacts with the rate limiter on the server. If you increase the retry count without increasing the delay, you can end up flooding the server during an outage. We learned that the hard way last year. Also note that the close handler runs on a different thread than the message handler, so any shared state needs a lock.

spoken: this function converts um a timestamp to the users local time zone it takes uh the offset from the user profile, not from the browser, um because we need the result to be consistent across devices note that daylight saving time um is handled by the library, so do not add one hour manually i made that mistake in the first version, er and it caused events to show up an hour early for half uh the year the unit tests cover the transitions um in march and november, no wait, march and october for the european zones er if you add a new region, add a test for its transition dates also, the function returns null for invalid offsets, so check the result before using it
intended: This function converts a timestamp to the user's local time zone. It takes the offset from the user profile, not from the browser, because we need the result to be consistent across devices. Note that daylight saving time is handled by the library, so do not add one hour manually. I made that mistake in the first version, and it caused events to show up an hour early for half the year. The unit tests cover the transitions in March and November, and in March and October for the European zones. If you add a new region, add a test for its transition dates. Also, the function returns null for invalid offsets, so check the result before using it.

Usage based plans are billed at the end of the cycle, based on the metered quantity. If a customer upgrades in the middle of a cycle, the system prorates the charge for the remaining days. Downgrades take effect at the start of the next cycle, to avoid issuing partial refunds. Invoices are generated on the last day of the month, and sent by email. Customers can download past invoices from the billing page, in PDF format. Failed payments are retried automatically three times over the following week. After that, the account is marked as past due, and access is restricted.

spoken: okay, a long explanation, um because this part confuses everyone the scheduler runs every minute, and uh it picks up jobs whose next run time is in the past it locks each job row so that two scheduler instances cannot run um the same job if a job takes longer than its interval, the next run is skipped, not queued we chose that on purpose, because queued runs piled up during um the outage in march and made recovery slower if you want different behavior for a particular job, uh add a flag, um do not change the default the lock times out after five minutes, no wait, after ten minutes, so a crashed worker does not block the job forever when you add a new job, register it in the jobs file and add a test that checks its schedule
intended: Okay, a long explanation, because this part confuses everyone. The scheduler runs every minute, and it picks up jobs whose next run time is in the past. It locks each job row so that two scheduler instances cannot run the same job. If a job takes longer than its interval, the next run is skipped, not queued. We chose that on purpose, because queued runs piled up during the outage in March and made recovery slower. If you want different behavior for a particular job, add a flag, do not change the default. spoken: this page describes the retention policy for logs and audit records application logs are kept for thirty days in hot storage and then moved to archive storage audit records are kept for seven years, actually, ten years for regulated customers, and they cannot be deleted by administrators if a customer asks for deletion under a privacy request, uh the records are anonymized rather than removed the anonymization job runs every night and processes requests in the order they were received you uh can check the status of um a request from uh the compliance dashboard requests normally finish within one day, uh but they er can take longer when uh the archive um is large if a request is stuck for more than three days, er contact the compliance team do not attempt to delete records manually, um because that can break the audit chain
intended: This page describes the retention policy for logs and audit records. Application logs are kept for 30 days in hot storage and then moved to archive storage. Audit records are kept for 10 years for regulated customers, and they cannot be deleted by administrators. If a customer asks for deletion under a privacy request, the records are anonymized rather than removed. The anonymization job runs every night and processes requests in the order they were received. You can check the status of a request from the compliance dashboard. Requests normally finish within one day, but they can take longer when the archive is large. If a request is stuck for more than three days, contact the compliance team. Do not attempt to delete records manually, because that can break the audit chain.

spoken: this one is subtle, so i will describe it carefully when two users edit the same document at the same time, the second save sometimes overwrites the first users changes without any warning we use optimistic locking, um so this should not happen, but it does, um roughly once in um a few hundred saves i dug into the code and found that the version check happens before uh the lock is acquired, not after so there is a window of about fifty milliseconds, no, about five hundred milliseconds under load, where both saves pass the check the fix is to move the check inside the transaction i have a patch ready, but i would like someone to review it carefully, because it touches the core save path i also wrote a test that reproduces the race by running two saves um in parallel the test fails before the patch um and passes after
intended: This one is subtle, so I will describe it carefully. When two users edit the same document at the same time, the second save sometimes overwrites the first user's changes without any warning. We use optimistic locking, so this should not happen, but it does, roughly once in a few hundred saves. I dug into the code and found that the version check happens before the lock is acquired, not after. So there is a window of about 500 milliseconds under load, where both saves pass the check. The fix is to move the check inside the transaction. I have a patch ready, but I would like someone to review it carefully, because it touches the core save path. I also wrote a test that reproduces the race by running two saves in parallel. The test fails before the patch and passes after.

intended: This class is a thin wrapper around the HTTP client, and its main job is to add authentication headers. It also handles refreshing expired tokens, which is the part that tends to break.
